title: Semantic diagram before visual layout
summary: Model the relationships and message of a diagram first, then choose a visual grammar that reveals those relationships with minimal decoration.
when_to_use: A technical concept is easier to understand through entities and connections than through prose alone.
avoid_when: A small table or a sentence conveys the same comparison more clearly.

anatomy.purpose: Names the few actors, components or states the reader must distinguish.
Represents direction, dependency, sequence or containment explicitly.
Highlights the main explanation while secondary detail recedes.
Explains visual encodings that are not self-evident.

tokens.name: --diagram-accent
tokens.purpose: One focal semantic role, not a generic decoration.

responsive: Split a large diagram into overview and detail when labels would be unreadable on a narrow screen.
accessibility: Provide a text summary of the diagram's meaning and preserve readable contrast and labels.
implementation_steps: Write the explanation as nodes and relations.
Select one diagram type matching the dominant relation.
Lay out the minimal readable set of nodes and provide a text equivalent.
